solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spooner's named boy, boy in crazy fashion

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two names trade places

parts.note: Mike is a boy's name
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent calls a boy by name, and he runs about wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the M of MIKE and the L of LAD gives LIKE MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'like mad' means frantically or wildly, as in a crazy manner.

clue.text: Animals slumbered uneasily without bed

indicators.note: sleeping uneasily is restless, so these letters are tossed about
the letters of the second word are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Animals slept fitfully with no bed to lie on.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, E, D out of SLUMBERED and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates of Madagascar, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Chemical's essential quality featured in report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a key note or tone is the dominant, essential quality of something

explanation.surface: A chemical's essential quality is mentioned in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY TONE said out loud sounds like the answer. The 's after 'Chemical' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketones are a class of organic compounds, acetone being the best known.

clue.text: Book collection and a thousand paintings maybe in extra arty city area

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for extra

parts.note: more means extra
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: A city's artistic quarter boasts a library and a thousand pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre is the hilltop district of Paris famed for its artists and painters.

clue.text: Hoi polloi in marches?

explanation.surface: The masses out on protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek for the people gives one sense; the short form of demonstrations gives the other.

clue.text: Movers exciting Don Quixote? Initially the old man dances

indicators.note: says that this part of the clue comes at the start, before the rest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man
the sails, or vanes, of windmills are the movers Don Quixote charged at, taking them for giants

explanation.surface: Something set Don Quixote off, while his father went dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote famously tilted at windmills, whose turning vanes stirred him to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavane is a slow, stately court dance of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Law enforcers on ship with soldiers who will make legal claim?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of what follows

parts.note: a posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff to enforce the law
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Lawmen board a ship with troops to stake a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner holding property is the party entitled to assert ownership in law.

clue.text: Container of drug that is nasty, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A medicine bottle holds something unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicines or liquids.

clue.text: Sweet dog lacking tail with leader at the front

indicators.note: says this piece goes before the rest

parts.note: No. 1, number one, is the leader

indicators.note: without its tail the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A sweet little dog with no tail runs behind the pack leader.
explanation.walkthrough: NO I is number one, read as letters; SETTER without its last letter gives SETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a chocolate made with hazelnuts, a kind of confection.

clue.text: Guide quietly leading the girl maybe into outhouse

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for outhouse

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding

indicators.note: the first piece goes ahead of the second

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
her refers to a girl, as one example of a female

explanation.surface: A guide quietly ushers a girl into a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to guide or herd them along.

clue.text: Havin' intimate relations in the morning

indicators.note: the clue spells this word with its final G dropped, inviting the same clipping of the next word

parts.note: mating is having sexual relations

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about lovemaking in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Havin'' is the signal: drop the G from MATING as the clue drops it from 'having'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matin, as an adjective, describes things belonging to the early part of the day, as in matin bells.

clue.text: What causes hallucinations? Claim seen to be false

indicators.note: a false version of these words has its letters set wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what produces visions and dismisses a reported sighting as untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescaline is a hallucinogenic drug obtained from the peyote cactus.

clue.text: Host needs to call maiden back, having been cut off prematurely

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: something cut off early loses its ending, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: astern means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A host must phone a young woman back, having been disconnected too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is ASTERN, which loses its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringmaster is the presenter who hosts and introduces the acts at a circus.

clue.text: Woman with upper hand, getting husband for daughter

indicators.note: the word for 'with upper hand' receives a new letter in place of an old one
the husband letter stands in for the daughter letter

parts.note: being in the lead means having the upper hand

explanation.surface: A woman holding the upper hand gets a husband for her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In LEAD, the D (daughter) is replaced by H (husband).
explanation.definitionFit: Leah, the wife of Jacob in Genesis, is a woman's name.

clue.text: Stars appearing after spring — see them on cricket fields

indicators.note: this piece comes after the next

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Stars come out after springtime, a sight above the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: On a cricket field, the boundaries are the rope edges where fours and sixes are scored.

clue.text: Nerdy type teaches Harry new tricks maybe

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's novels

explanation.surface: A geek shows the young wizard some new magic tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new tricks maybe' just adds to the picture of teaching: a trainer teaches new tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collects locomotive numbers is the stereotype of an obsessive, nerdy hobbyist.

clue.text: At home with minimal cash, the setter has motivation

parts.note: in means at home
a cent is a tiny amount of money
the setter writing would say I've, I have

explanation.surface: At home with little money, the crossword setter is driven to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is a spur or inducement that motivates someone.

clue.text: Flourish as scoundrel with dreadful clue one penned

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: one is penned inside the jumbled letters
a dreadful version of the word is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A setter boasts as a rogue who wrote a terrible clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' turns CLUE into LCUE, and 'penned' puts I inside it to make LICUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A curlicue is a decorative curl or twist in handwriting or design, a flourish.

clue.text: Recommending a holy condition, I render hymn perhaps

parts.note: taken as written
DV, Deo volente, means God willing, a pious condition on a plan
taken as written
to sing is to render, or perform, a hymn, for example

explanation.surface: Offering advice: God willing, I will perform a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Advising someone means recommending a course of action to them.

clue.text: Emphasising what a consistently poor batsman is doing?

definitions.text: what a consistently poor batsman is doing?
definitions.meaning: a batsman who keeps making few runs is scoring below par

explanation.definitionFit: Underlining a word stresses it; read literally, the word means making too few runs.

clue.text: Case of fruit placed outside Roman square

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a date is a fruit
four, the square of two, is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A box of fruit is set out in a Roman piazza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a plaza; it is the number four, two squared.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is the grammatical case for an indirect object.

clue.text: Like a lads' party journalist organised

parts.note: a stag do or stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist arranged a men-only party.
explanation.walkthrough: A STAG party is the British name for a groom's pre-wedding night out with his male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage an event is to arrange or put it on.

clue.text: Put down using language that's heartless

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses another with heartless words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes T, the middle letter of LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lain is the past participle of lie, so 'put down' as in having been laid to rest or placed.

clue.text: Ghastly and horribly pale? Get suntan relaxing outside

indicators.note: one set of rearranged letters goes around the other
relaxing these letters loosens their order, so they are rearranged
something done horribly is mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a horribly pale person: go and relax outdoors to get a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' turns SUNTAN into UNSANT, which goes 'outside' PLEA, made from PALE by 'horribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly and disagreeable are near-synonyms, both describing something nasty.

clue.text: City with modern lights, minimal energy being consumed

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, taken inside the other piece

parts.note: LEDs, light-emitting diodes, are modern lamps
E is the physics symbol for energy, a single letter

explanation.surface: A city fitted with new lighting uses very little power.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Mark loses heart in a state of stupor

indicators.note: losing its heart, the word drops one of its middle letters

parts.note: a comma is a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: Mark grows dispirited and sinks into torpor.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a deep state of unconsciousness, beyond mere stupor.

clue.text: Garment an abomination putting me off — no brand to follow

indicators.note: says this piece comes after what precedes it
with 'off', tells us to take the given letters away
putting something off removes it, here from the word for an abomination

parts.note: a crime is an outrage or abomination
taken as written
taken as written
a line is a brand of product range

explanation.surface: A garment so hideous it put me off, with no designer label to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIME loses ME to leave CRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline is a stiff petticoat that held out the wide skirts of Victorian dresses.

clue.text: Top layer in old British firm no good

parts.note: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British company

explanation.surface: The top tier at an old British firm is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of a cake.

clue.text: Avenger somehow settled score

indicators.note: letters settled in some other way are rearranged

explanation.surface: An avenger finally settled an old score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled score' looks like the idiom for revenge; only 'score' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, which is what engraving does.

clue.text: Our group, going into shed, stop for a while

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to shed money is to spend it, to let it go
us is the group we belong to

explanation.surface: Our group heads into a shed and pauses for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to halt it temporarily.
